text:
[NTST.6.1] Testing a TTL means testing a boundary, so the test has to land on
both sides of it.

A fact's deadline is fixed when the fact is asserted -- the clock at that
moment plus the TTL -- and does not move afterwards ([NTST.3.5]). The
comparison against it is **inclusive**: a pump with the clock one tick short
of the deadline leaves the fact alive, and a pump with the clock exactly at
the deadline retracts it. A test that checks only the far side proves the fact
eventually dies, not that it dies when it should.

The retraction is the pump's work rather than the clock's ([NTST.3.4]), which
is why each half of the check is a clock move, then a pump, then a count.
